text:
[LTAC.5.3] A missed tick — when the engine is paused, sleeping,
or otherwise unable to evaluate during a scheduled tick — must
not skip the timer firing. The follow-up rule's LHS uses
`monotonic_ns() >= t.fire_at`, which holds on every later tick; the
follow-up fires late, never lost. The guard is `>=` against an
absolute instant rather than equality against a scheduled one,
and that is the whole mechanism — an equality test would lose
exactly the tick this clause is about.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__guard_expr
idris.note: `>=` against the absolute instant, as the clause requires, written on the `dwell` leaf. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__guard_is_due
idris.note: `>=` against the absolute instant `stamp + dur`, carried through: what the `dwell` guard decides is what the clause's guard decides.

idris.name: ltac_5_3__lte_is_lte_b
idris.note: The two Boolean orders on naturals -- the Prelude's `lte`, which the `dwell` gate uses, and Rete/TmsRun.idr's `lte_b`, which the timer's `fire_at` gate uses -- are one function. By induction.
